voyage.name: Military Museum
voyage.content: Extensive collection of Serbia's military history. Good signage in English.

voyage.name: Belgrade Zoo
voyage.content: Popular, but with a lot of animals in a small space.

voyage.name: Belgrade Cathedral
voyage.content: The Cathedral Church of St Michael the Archangel is Orthodox, built 1837-40 in neoclassical style with a richly-decorated interior. Buried in front of the church are two notable Serbian linguists, Vuk Karadžić and Dositej Obradović.

voyage.name: Museum of the Serbian Orthodox Church
voyage.content: Museum of church history with frescoes, mosaics, and icons. Good signage in English.

voyage.name: Residence of Princess Ljubica
voyage.content: Built in 1830 as a grand residence for Ljubica Vukomanović (1788-1843), consort of Prince Miloš Obrenović. It remained in royal use to 1842. Since 1979 it's been a branch of the City Museum, exhibiting architecture and furnishings of the 19th century, when Serbia was in transition from Ottoman to European styles.

voyage.name: Museum of Applied Art
voyage.content: Displaying art and design from early history.

voyage.name: Zepter Museum
voyage.content: Modern Serbian art.

voyage.name: Ethnographic Museum
voyage.content: Extensive display of Serbian costumes, tools, culture and everyday life in past centuries.

voyage.name: Bajrakli Mosque
voyage.content: Built around 1575 when Islam was the majority religion, it's now the only mosque in Belgrade. Bajrakli means "with flag" - the muwaqqit calculated the exact time of Islamic observances and hoisted a flag to advise the other city mosques, whereupon each muezzin called from their minaret to those within earshot. It's been smashed up several times, most recently in 2004 during the Kosovo conflict, but restored.

voyage.name: Chocolate Museum
voyage.content: Chocolate's role in the story of the city, and you get to make your own.

voyage.name: Museum of Science and Technology
voyage.content: Gadgets, transport and machinery down the ages.

voyage.name: Church of St Alexander Nevsky
voyage.content: This Orthodox church was completed in 1929, replacing that of 1877. It has notable relics and frescoes.

voyage.name: National Museum
voyage.hours: Tue Wed Fri Sun 10:00-18:00, Thu Sat 12:00-20:00
voyage.content: Founded in 1844, it has more than 400,000 items on 3 floors. It's organised into Paleolithic, Ancient History, Middle Ages and Modern.

voyage.name: Republic Square
voyage.content: The south side of the National Museum is the city's main plaza. The equestrian statue is of Prince Mihailo Obrenović (1823-1868), who negotiated the withdrawal of Ottoman troops from Belgrade. The city Cultural Centre also fronts onto the square. In spite of the imposing buildings, it's a drab concrete expanse thronged with traffic along Francuska.

voyage.name: Sukat Shalom Synagogue
voyage.content: Sephardic Jews settled in Belgrade from the 16th century, as the Ottomans welcomed those fleeing Spanish persecution. The Ashkenazis arrived in numbers from the 19th century, escaping Tsarist Russia, and completed this synagogue in 1924. It's still active, but now closed to visitors because of the risk of attack. (It's the same story with the Jewish Museum at Kralja Petra 71a.)

voyage.name: Museum of Illusions
voyage.content: Family-friendly place with all the fairground usuals: distorting mirrors, Ames Room, and so on.

voyage.name: Old Palace
voyage.content: This was the residence of the Obrenović and Karađorđević princely dynasties from 1884 until 1922. It now houses Belgrade City Assembly, no visits except on business.

voyage.name: Ivo Andric Museum
voyage.content: Museum in the home of Nobel laureate Ivo Andric (1892-1975).

voyage.name: Historical Museum of Serbia
voyage.content: Huge collection of materials about the Serbian nation from ancient times to the present. In the coming years it's intended to move to new premises on the site of the former railway station.

voyage.name: National Assembly of Serbia
voyage.content: Grand neo-baroque legislative palace, built 1907-36.

voyage.name: St Mark's Church
voyage.alt: Crkva Sv Marka / Црква Св Марка
voyage.content: Large Serbian Orthodox church built 1931-40 in Serbo-Byzantine style. Within are the tombs of King Stefan Uroš IV Dušan (1308-55), and of King Aleksandar I Obrenović (1876-1903) and his Queen Draga Mašin.

voyage.name: Nikola Tesla Museum
voyage.price: English guided tour RSD800, cash only
voyage.content: Nikola Tesla (Никола Тесла, 1856-1943) made huge contributions to electric engineering, pioneering alternating current (enabling long-distance high-energy transfer), radio (underpinning today's mobile comms) and AC motors as used in household and office machinery. Half of this small museum is dedicated to Tesla's personal effects, while the other half contains models of his inventions. English-speaking tours start at

voyage.name: Temple of Saint Sava
voyage.alt: Hram Svetog Save / Храм Светог Саве
voyage.content: The largest church in Serbia and one of the largest Orthodox churches in the world, under construction since 1935 and still not entirely finished. It's described as a temple (Hram) to distinguish it from the smaller St Sava Church (Tsrkva) adjacent. The crypt (downstairs from the main entrance) is an extensive, bright and polished area with walls covered with modern iconography, so it looks more like a metro intercha

voyage.name: Cathedral of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary
Church of the Intercession of the Holy Virgin
voyage.content: Small Orthodox church built in 1933, in simple Serbian-Byzantine style. It's adorned with frescoes and mosaics, and has a rich collection of relics.

voyage.name: Presentation of the Virgin Monastery
voyage.content: Orthodox monastery church built in 1935 in the Serbian-Byzantine style.

voyage.name: Museum of Yugoslavia and Tito's Mausoleum
voyage.content: This is in 3 buildings. Old Museum is a general display of the history and culture of the former Yugoslavia. 25 May Museum is an oh-so-Sixties building named for the official birthdate of Josip Broz Tito (1892-1980). It displays presents given to him during his 27-year presidency: he amassed quite a collection of youth relay batons. House of Flowers is his mausoleum.

voyage.name: Museum of African Art
voyage.content: West African contemporary art.

voyage.name: Royal Palace
voyage.content: Residence of the royal family of Serbia. You can only visit on a guided tour (in English or Serbian), booked through the Tourist Information Offices. The tour takes in the White Palace, with a large art collection.

voyage.name: Banjica concentration camp
voyage.content: This operated from July 1941 to October 1944 under Gestapo leadership; at least 3849 perished here. It's now a museum.

voyage.name: Rakovica Monastery
voyage.content: Built on its present site from 1600, the monastery's main structure is the Church of Archangel Michael. The other churches are modern.

voyage.name: White Hill
voyage.hours: Apr-Oct Tue Wed Fri 10:00-16:00, Thu 12:00-18:00, Sat Sun 10:00-18:00
voyage.content: A large tell, a 10 m hillock of prehistoric settlements, mostly Neolithic. At weekends there are guided tours through the site.

voyage.name: Museum of Contemporary Art
voyage.content: Large museum of Yugoslav, Serbian and international art of the 20th century, in a striking modern building.

voyage.name: Aeronautical Museum
voyage.content: Closed for rebuilding until 2027. The main collection is in a striking geodesic glass building, with additional aircraft displayed on the surrounding grounds. The museum has over 200 aircraft flown by the Serbian and Yugoslav Air Forces, aero clubs and private & commercial aviation, from gliders to helicopters to jet fighters. There are a number of rare aircraft and other aviation equipment. The museum also displays

voyage.name: Chinese Cultural Centre, Belgrade
voyage.content: A cultural centre built on the former site of the Chinese embassy to Yugoslavia, which was bombed by NATO forces in a so-called miscalculated operation in 1999. There is a plaque commemorating the Chinese journalists who died in the bombing.

voyage.name: Public Observatory
voyage.content: Four small telescopes enable daytime viewing of the city. On F Sa evenings from 20:30 if the sky is clear you can use the 110/2050 mm refractor and 200/2000 mm reflector for night viewing, with commentary and guidance from staff. The regular observatory is 3 km southeast in Zvezdara Park, and occasionally has guided tours.

voyage.name: National Theatre
voyage.content: This puts on opera, ballet and theatre. The main hall is worth looking in at, decorated with gilt and artwork.

voyage.name: KMN
voyage.content: Great selection of domestic cuisine, including veggie. Friendly efficient staff.

voyage.name: Roll Bar
voyage.content: Good quality, sizable portions. Try the imperial chicken and feta chicken.

voyage.name: Pizzeria Trg
voyage.content: Delicious pizza and pancakes. Cash only.

voyage.name: Yalla Yalla
voyage.content: Lebanese food.

voyage.name: Skadarlijske kobasice
voyage.content: Excellent sausages.

voyage.name: Giros tim
voyage.content: Good gyros.

voyage.name: Amigo
voyage.content: Very good fried pancakes.

voyage.name: Gastroteka
voyage.content: Serbian fast food.

voyage.name: Jazzayoga
voyage.content: Sandwiches, wraps, juices, and baked goods, relaxing ambience.

voyage.name: Orašac
voyage.content: A garden restaurant with trad Serbian cuisine.

voyage.name: Šešir moj
voyage.content: The hats are the natty boaters of the quartet, who riff away with barcarolles and other crowd-pleasers. Good hearty Serbian fare.

voyage.name: Znak Pitanja
voyage.content: Traditional Serbian cuisine. Try ćevapčići sa kajmakom (grilled minced meat with cream), or if you have an adventurous stomach, try young bull's sex glands & bowels.

voyage.name: Loki
voyage.content: Pljeskavici are Serbian burgers. Variety of toppings like spicy cheese or pickled peppers.

voyage.name: Mika Alas
voyage.content: Try their delicious fish soup "riblja čorba" and their house specialty, "smuđ romanov", Pike Perch fillet in white wine cream sauce. Excellent food for an acceptable price.

voyage.name: Makao i Žuto More
voyage.content: Good Chinese food. They also have branches at Pere Velimirovića 7 downtown and Starine Novaka 7a near Tašmajdan Park.

voyage.name: Moon Sushi
voyage.content: Mostly good reviews for their sushi.

voyage.name: Marukoshi
voyage.content: Japanese restaurant with good-ish reviews.

voyage.name: Zapata
voyage.content: Friendly place for authentic Mexican fare.

voyage.name: Botako
voyage.content: Good scores for Italian cuisine and ambiance. There's another branch south at Nevesinjska 6.

voyage.name: Casa Nova
voyage.content: Good Franco-Italian fare with ample portions.

voyage.name: Restoran Caruso
voyage.content: Italian restaurant on 8th floor, with views over Terazije, river Sava and Novi Belgrade.

voyage.name: Sinđelić
voyage.content: Traditional Serbian cuisine.

voyage.name: Šaran
voyage.content: Riverside fish restaurant with live trad music.

voyage.name: Lorenzo & Kakalamba
voyage.content: Italian and southeastern Serbian cuisine, but mostly you come for the way-out decor, which is beyond kitsch.

voyage.name: Blaznavac
voyage.content: Courtyard café-bar with eclectic decoration, serving cocktails, beer and coffee.

voyage.name: Demokratija bar
voyage.content: Cocktail and wine bar serving cocktails and house infusions, with a smoke-free interior and outdoor seating.

voyage.name: Riddle Bar
voyage.content: Speakeasy-style cocktail bar without a fixed menu; bartenders suggest drinks based on the guest's preferences.

voyage.name: Black Turtle
voyage.content: One of several Black Turtle brewery pubs. House beers include fruit-flavoured variants; this branch has outdoor tables with river views.

voyage.name: Dogma Brewery Central
voyage.content: Brewery taproom with eight rotating taps, canned releases, bar food and a small courtyard.

voyage.name: Gecko
voyage.content: Irish-style pub on the central pedestrian café strip.

voyage.name: Publin
voyage.content: Small neighbourhood pub with rock music and Serbian beer.

voyage.name: Three Carrots Irish Pub
voyage.content: Irish pub with draft beer, televised sport and occasional live or acoustic music.

voyage.name: Zuzu's
voyage.content: Café-bar and kitchen with outdoor tables on Obilićev Venac.

voyage.name: Hostel 360
voyage.content: Cosy hostel just off Republic Square.

voyage.name: Hostelche
voyage.content: Clean, cozy place. They have free sheets, towels, laundry, games, books, Wi-Fi, welcome drink, coffee, and tea.

voyage.name: Sun Hostel
voyage.content: Well-run hostel, clean and spacious, with dorms, apt & private rooms. Comfy, a/c, safe-lockers backpack size, free internet, friendly staff.

voyage.name: Fair and Square Hostel
voyage.content: Comfy rooms, large kitchen and public area as well as patio, friendly staff, cat and dog.

voyage.name: Balkan Soul Hostel
voyage.content: Small but very social and cozy hostel with a well-equipped shared guest kitchen and lounge. Rooms have good air conditioning and wi-fi.

voyage.name: ArkaBarka Floating Hostel
voyage.content: Friendly floating hostel on the Danube, with an on-board cafe-bar and sauna.

voyage.name: San Art Floating Hostel
voyage.content: Is it a chalet, is it a houseboat? Clean, well-run, friendly hostel near river confluence.

voyage.name: The Horse Monument Hostel
voyage.content: A small hostel in the Old Town, close to Skadarlija bohemic neighborhood.

voyage.name: Belgrade City Hotel
voyage.content: Central hotel in Neo-Renaissance building, with gym, restaurant and bar.

voyage.name: Villa Forever
voyage.content: Basic place near Brankov Bridge.

voyage.name: Slavija Hotel
voyage.content: Basic but central. On-site business center and sauna. The rooftop restaurant serves breakfast.

voyage.name: Hotel Srbija
voyage.content: This weary old Soviet tower is where Air Serbia will put you if you miss a connection. Large restaurant on the 18th floor.

voyage.name: Mercure Belgrade Excelsior
voyage.content: Decent mid-town Accor chain hotel, rooms equipped with TV, mini-refrigerators, workspaces, and Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Royal Inn
voyage.content: One of the oldest hotels in Belgrade, dating to 1885, gets positive reviews. Rooms are small, but renovated and furnished with TV, air conditioning and mini-bar.

voyage.name: Nevski Hotel
voyage.content: Comfortable central hotel, with business services and a good breakfast buffet.

voyage.name: Design Hotel Mr President
voyage.content: Comfortable modern hotel, 61 rooms with internet and standard facilities.

voyage.name: Queen's Astoria Design Hotel
voyage.content: Central hotel with bistro.

voyage.name: Hotel Rex
voyage.content: Comfy, central business-type hotel.

voyage.name: Putnik Inn
voyage.content: Decent 3 star business hotel.

voyage.name: Belgrade Art Hotel
voyage.content: Boutique hotel in very central spot, now part of Radisson chain. With 55 rooms and suites, bar, lounge bar, restaurant and 2 meeting rooms.

voyage.name: Townhouse 27
voyage.content: Clean efficient 4-star in city centre.

voyage.name: Crystal Hotel
voyage.content: Decent hotel with 44 rooms.

voyage.name: Balkan Hotel
voyage.content: Central functional hotel.

voyage.name: Moskva
voyage.content: Upmarket hotel in a landmark building. Rooms are stylish but small, and tall visitors should avoid the fifth floor, where the pitch of the roof closes in. Helpful multilingual staff. Excellent breakfast, with the piano tinkling over the eggs and pâtisserie - now this is what you call café society! (Especially with limited mobility, since you can enter via the café at street level and avoid the steps to the main hotel

voyage.name: Hyatt Regency
voyage.content: Big four star on west bank, spacious comfy rooms.

voyage.name: Crowne Plaza
voyage.content: Big glassy business hotel on the west bank, with fitness center and conference facilities, connected by passageway to the Sava congress & retail center.

voyage.name: IN Hotel Belgrade
voyage.content: Boxy 4-star on west bank, good reviews for comfort & facilities. 200 m from Kombank Arena, handy for riverside life and highway out to airport.
